subject: Bridging strategy for Private Deploy: shortlists for Peering / PrivateLink / S2S
messages:

Cc: netops-team@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ingress path options — peering vs privatelink vs s2s (initial)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning. We're trying to finalize the recommended ingress pattern for our Private deployment with Redwood: we need something that meets our compliance and throughput needs but keeps operational overhead manageable. High level constraints:
- Bulk inference traffic will be ~3-5 Gbps sustained, spiking to 10 Gbps during batch windows.
- We need auditability (flow logs + signed request paths) and ability to rotate keys via our HSM.
- Network team prefers minimal route table churn across multiple AZs.

Can you shoot over a succinct comparison with your recommendation? If you have a topology sketch in PNG/PDF format that highlights control-plane vs data-plane, that'd be helpful.

Appreciate it — Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Analytics
[sanjay.patel@acmeanalytics.com]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress path options — peering vs privatelink vs s2s (initial)

Hi Sanjay — thanks, and good constraints. Attached a quick topology and a bridging matrix (bridging-matrix-20260830.pdf) that summarizes operational tradeoffs. Short answer upfront: for your profile I recommend a dual-path approach — PrivateLink for control-plane and metadata (smaller, low-latency calls) and S2S VPN for bulk payloads, with an option to replace S2S with an interface endpoint/privatelink path later if you decide to standardize on AWS-managed endpoints.

Quick rationale:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints):
  • Pros: preserves AWS-native security boundary, no public IP exposure for control plane; easier to manage per-AZ; integrates with VPC endpoint policies for strict access.
  • Cons: egress pricing for large payloads can be material; operationally you end up managing endpoint ENIs per AZ.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPSEC):
  • Pros: simple routing model, works across clouds/on-prem, predictable per-byte pricing on your side, fewer AWS-specific objects.
  • Cons: latency variability for long-haul links; need to manage tunnels and HA (we typically recommend dual tunnels with BGP).
- VPC peering:
  • Pros: low-latency, low-cost intra-region; straightforward for single-account, single-VPC setups.
  • Cons: doesn't scale well across many VPCs/accounts; peering requires route table entries in both VPCs and can become brittle as the number of partners grows.

Operational note: given your need for HSM key rotations and auditability, we'd put authentication on top of both paths: mTLS with client certs pinned to your KMS/HSM, and token-level audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. Also recommend enabling Flow Logs + VPC Endpoint logs (for PrivateLink) so you have visibility per-path.

I've attached a sketched topology (acme_vpc_topology.png) that shows control plane to PrivateLink (low bandwidth, high auditability) and bulk to a high-bandwidth S2S tunnel. If you want, Marcus and I can walk through a short decision rubric on Tuesday to pick which path to pilot.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park

On Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 10:05 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sanjay — thanks, and good constraints. Attached a quick topology and a bridging matrix...
> Short answer upfront: ... dual-path approach — PrivateLink for control-plane and metadata and S2S for bulk payloads...

Adding a few concrete tradeoffs / config knobs from the runtime side that matter for your decision:

1) Latency SLOs vs Cost:
   - If your app requires p50 < 30ms for chat-style inference, PrivateLink for inference calls (not just control) is preferable even with higher per-GB cost.
   - For batch jobs or higher throughput pipelines where per-GB cost dominates, S2S (or direct peering if intra-account) reduces unit cost.

2) Batching and KV cache behavior:
   - Our runtime benefits from stable low-latency connections because it sustains KV cache hits and continuous batching. Intermittent jitter on S2S can erode batching efficiency; recommend tuning aggressive keepalives and using managed BGP hold timers.

3) High-availability pattern we typically deploy here:
   - Control-plane: multi-AZ PrivateLink endpoints, with endpoint policies restricting to your subnet CIDRs.
   - Data-plane: dual S2S tunnels (primary to our nearest edge POP, secondary to a second POP/region). Route metrics prefer the low-latency path; fall back automatically on failover.

4) Security and compliance:
   - We can enforce mTLS and client cert rotations every 90 days; we recommend integrating cert issuance with your HSM-backed CA.
   - For audit, enable both VPC Flow Logs (to S3) and publish endpoint logs to your logging collector. We can provide a mapping of log fields to SOC2 control families if that helps procurement.

5) Migration path: start with dual-path then test converting S2S bulk to PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for one AZ to measure egress cost delta and latency. If costs are acceptable, you can standardize on PrivateLink for simpler routing and better latency.

Action items I propose:
- Redwood: produce an HA config template (BGP + PSKs, MTU tuning, tunnel monitoring) — ETA Wed 9/2.
- Acme: provide current egress pricing and confirmation of HSM CA/PKI workflow so we can draft cert rotation steps.

Happy to jump on the call with Marcus to map this to your infra runbook.

— Priyom
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: bridging-matrix-20260830.pdf already shared]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress path options — peering vs privatelink vs s2s (decision + next steps)

Thanks everyone — concise decision following the notes above.

Decision: Pilot dual-path (PrivateLink for control-plane + S2S for bulk) for 30 days. Success criteria:
- End-to-end p95 latency for control plane < 60ms across AZs.
- Sustained bulk throughput >= 3 Gbps on S2S with <1% packet loss.
- Visibility: Flow logs + endpoint logs available in Acme's SIEM within 15 minutes.
- Cost: incremental egress cost during pilot capped at $X/month (we'll align with procurement).

Next steps / schedule:
- Action (Redwood): deliver HA S2S template and BGP config (Priyom) — target Wed 2026-09-02.
- Action (Acme): share HSM CA process + egress pricing by Tue 2026-09-01.
- Pilot kickoff: Thurs 2026-09-03 — 1-hour runbook walkthrough and smoke tests.

If the pilot shows stable latency and acceptable cost we'll keep S2S for data-plane and consider migrating some high-frequency inference endpoints to PrivateLink in Q4.

Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference
